probes.question: In dollar-cost averaging, what stays fixed each period?
True or false: dollar-cost averaging means buying the same number of shares each period.

image.alt: An early Edison stock ticker under a glass dome, with a paper tape wheel and a ring of small keys.

body.question: You invest the same $100 every month. In a month when the share price is low, what happens to the number of shares your $100 buys?
body.reveal: More. A fixed amount of money buys more shares when the price is low and fewer when it is high, which is the idea behind dollar-cost averaging. The investor decides only how much to invest and how often, which is why it often runs automatically, such as through payroll deductions.
